'''David George Lloyd''' (born 25 April 1974) is an Irish&ndash;Australian chemist and university administrator. He became the [[List of Australian university leaders|youngest vice-chancellor in Australia]] when he was appointed in 2013, at the age of 38.

Born in [[Dublin]], Ireland, Lloyd studied applied chemistry at [[Dublin City University]] and completed a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in medicinal [[organic chemistry]], followed by a [[Master of Arts]] from [[Trinity College Dublin]]. After postdoctoral research and work in the pharmaceutical industry, he joined De Novo Pharmaceuticals in [[Cambridge]] in 2001 and returned to Trinity College Dublin in 2004, where he held several academic and administrative positions, including Dean and Vice President of Research from 2007 to 2011. In 2012, he became chair of the [[Irish Research Council]] and was involved in national science and innovation policy.

Lloyd was appointed [[List of University of South Australia people#Vice-Chancellors|Vice Chancellor and President]] of the [[University of South Australia]] (UniSA) on 22 August 2012, and commenced in early 2013. At 38, he became Australia's youngest vice-chancellor. During his tenure, he oversaw UniSA's strategic and capital development programs, including the development of Pridham Hall and the Health Innovation Building, and established partnerships with industry and universities in Australia and overseas. He also served on the boards of the [[South Australian Health and Medical Research Institute]] and the state's [[Economic Development Board (South Australia)|Economic Development Board]], and was appointed to the [[Australian Research Council]] Advisory Council in 2018. In 2018, Lloyd initiated discussions with the [[University of Adelaide]] (UofA) about a possible merger, although the negotiations ended without agreement later that year.

In 2022, Lloyd and [[Peter Høj]] proposed merging UniSA with UofA to establish [[Adelaide University]] (AU). The merger was approved in 2023 and AU was established on 8 March 2024, with Lloyd and Høj serving as co-vice chancellors during the transition. Lloyd was also chair of [[Universities Australia]] from 2023 to 2025. In that same year, he and Høj announced that they would not seek appointment as AU's inaugural substantive vice-chancellor, and [[Nicola Phillips]] commenced in the role in early 2026. Lloyd concluded the operations of UniSA at the end of March 2026 and left university management of the merger, establishing [https://www.bluerange.com.au/ BlueRange Advisory].{{citation needed|date=August 2026}} In [https://www.notredame.edu.au/news-items/appointment-of-interim-vice-chancellor September 2026] Lloyd was announced as the Interim Vice Chancellor of the [[University of Notre Dame Australia]]. 

== Early life and education ==
David George Lloyd was born on 25 April 1974 in [[Dublin]], Ireland,<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Hare |first=Julie |date=2013-02-27 |title=Lloyd's mix of Irish chemistry to lift UniSA |url=https://www.theaustralian.com.au/higher-education/lloyds-mix-of-irish-chemistry-to-lift-unisa/news-story/bed6be440d02ad8ac35a03ceb74e6854?amp |url-access=subscription |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=[[The Australian]]}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=McCarthy |first=Gavan |date=2025-08-18 |title=Lloyd, David |url=https://www.eoas.info/biogs/P007819b.htm |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=[[Encyclopedia of Australian Science and Innovation]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260818003840/https://www.eoas.info/biogs/P007819b.htm|archive-date=2026-08-18}}</ref> and became the first member of his family to attend university.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Tim |date=2016-06-25 |title=From part-time Dublin music store worker to UniSA Vice-Chancellor — meet David Lloyd |url=https://www.adelaidenow.com.au/lifestyle/sa-weekend/from-parttime-dublin-music-store-worker-to-unisa-vicechancellor--meet-david-lloyd/news-story/f07f8941e05a3d52a5e832bde66b44b6 |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=[[The Advertiser (Adelaide)|The Advertiser]]}}</ref> He studied [[applied chemistry]] at [[Dublin City University]], where he graduated with a [[Bachelor of Science]] ([[Honours degree|Honours]]) and later completed a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in medicinal [[organic chemistry]],<ref name=":4" /> researching [[Antimalarial medication|antimalarial compounds]]. During his undergraduate studies, he worked part-time at Waltons music store in Dublin and undertook an internship with the Irish division of the Dutch pharmaceutical company [[Organon]], where he worked in quality assurance.<ref name=":3" /> He subsequently obtained a [[Master of Arts]] from [[Trinity College Dublin]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Prof David Lloyd |url=https://www.atn.edu.au/team-members/prof-david-lloyd/ |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=[[Australian Technology Network|Australian Technology Network of Universities]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250122141012/https://www.atn.edu.au/team-members/prof-david-lloyd/|archive-date=2025-01-22}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
Following his doctoral studies, Lloyd undertook [[postdoctoral research]] at Trinity College Dublin, where his research focused on [[molecular modelling]] and [[computer-aided drug design]].<ref name=":3" /> He subsequently worked in the pharmaceutical industry in the United Kingdom and,<ref name=":4" /> in 2001, joined [[Cambridge]]-based start-up De Novo Pharmaceuticals as a senior scientist. He returned to Trinity College Dublin in 2004 as a senior lecturer and was appointed Associate Dean of Research in 2005. He later became head of the Molecular Design Group<ref name=":1" /> and served as Dean and Vice President of Research from 2007 to 2011, before becoming Bursar and Director of Strategic Innovation. In these roles, he was involved in Trinity's research and development strategy, including funding for the Trinity Biomedical Sciences Institute, and served on the National Advisory Council for Science, Technology and Innovation and a subgroup of the [[Taoiseach]]'s Innovation Task Force.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |date=2012-08-22 |title=A new vice-chancellor has been appointed at the University of South Australia |url=https://www.theaustralian.com.au/higher-education/a-new-vicechancellor-has-been-appointed-at-the-university-of-south-australia-/news-story/bebe43cd9bfe21c098c82d02d9e6b05e?amp |url-access=subscription |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=The Australian}}</ref> In March 2012, he became chair of the [[Irish Research Council]],<ref name=":3" /> having previously served as its first chair.<ref name=":1" /> Lloyd supported the Innovation Alliance and the establishment of a national innovation task force in Ireland during the post-[[2008 financial crisis|2008 economic downturn]].<ref name=":10">{{Cite web |last=Evans |first=Richard |date=2014-06-28 |title=UniSA vice chancellor David Lloyd joins the new Economic Development Board next week |url=https://www.adelaidenow.com.au/business/sa-business-journal/unisa-vice-chancellor-david-lloyd-joins-the-new-economic-development-board-next-week/news-story/4ece4aa44895d2a4ac68279bb9e06d34 |url-access=subscription |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=The Advertiser}}</ref>

== University career ==
=== University of South Australia (2013–2022/2026) ===
On 22 August 2012, Lloyd was appointed [[List of University of South Australia people#Vice-Chancellors|Vice Chancellor and President]] of the [[University of South Australia]] (UniSA), commencing in early 2013<ref name=":6" /> and succeeding [[Peter Høj]].<ref name=":8">{{Cite news |title=University Merger Promises Transformational Opportunities for South Australia |url=https://sponsored.chronicle.com/university-merger-promises-transformational-opportunities-for-south-australia/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260416230100/https://sponsored.chronicle.com/university-merger-promises-transformational-opportunities-for-south-australia/ |archive-date=2026-04-16 |access-date=2026-07-17 |work=[[The Chronicle of Higher Education]]}}</ref> He relocated to Adelaide in 2013 and,<ref name=":3" /> at 38, became Australia's youngest vice-chancellor.<ref name=":0" /> In February, he identified [[student–teacher ratio]]s and the student experience as areas of focus and directed a research collaboration with [[Tianjin University]] on sustainable urban development, with [[A$]]1 million in funding provided by each university.<ref name=":1" /> In May, he confirmed that UniSA was developing plans for a major presence on [[North Terrace, Adelaide|North Terrace]] near the new [[Royal Adelaide Hospital]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2013-05-21 |title=UniSA plans health hub on North Tce |url=https://www.indailysa.com.au/news/archive/2013/05/21/unisa-plans-health-hub-on-north-tce |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=[[InDaily]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260818004134/https://www.indailysa.com.au/news/archive/2013/05/21/unisa-plans-health-hub-on-north-tce|archive-date=2026-08-18}}</ref> In August, he released a five-year plan that included evaluating two-year professional [[master's degrees]] in selected disciplines following three-year [[bachelor's degree]]s, with physiotherapy, [[occupational therapy]] and education identified as possible areas for consideration.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Trounson |first=Andrew |date=2013-08-16 |title=UniSA flags part shift to professional masters, seeks 100 new professors |url=https://www.theaustralian.com.au/higher-education/unisa-flags-part-shift-to-professional-masters-seeks-100-new-professors/news-story/a27ec9faeac187cd526f3cc5b040b90d?amp |url-access=subscription |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=The Australian}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Schriever |first=Jordanna |date=2013-11-26 |title=All new South Australian teachers will need Master degrees in shake-up of education standards |url=https://www.news.com.au/national/south-australia/all-new-south-australian-teachers-will-need-master-degrees-in-shakeup-of-education-standards/news-story/c465dea41e6549e47da4f8f04496d35d |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=[[News.com.au]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180907220223/https://www.news.com.au/national/south-australia/all-new-south-australian-teachers-will-need-master-degrees-in-shakeup-of-education-standards/news-story/c465dea41e6549e47da4f8f04496d35d|archive-date=2018-09-07}}</ref> The plan also included a cancer biology centre, a new [[great hall]] and other infrastructure developments across UniSA's four campuses.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-01-24 |title=Neither SuperTAFE nor sandstone: UniSA's global ambition |url=https://www.indailysa.com.au/news/archive/2014/01/24/unisas-global-vision-neither-supertafe-sandstone |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=InDaily|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260818004334/https://www.indailysa.com.au/news/archive/2014/01/24/unisas-global-vision-neither-supertafe-sandstone|archive-date=2026-08-18}}</ref>
[[File:The Høj Plaza on the Adelaide University City Campus West, May 2026 (DSCF7215).jpg|left|thumb|Pridham Hall (left), Høj Plaza (centre), and Jeffrey Smart Building (right) in 2026]]
Lloyd was appointed to the [[South Australian Health and Medical Research Institute]] board on 29 November 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Annual Report 2014 |url=https://sahmri.blob.core.windows.net/communications/sahmri.org/Annual_Report_2014.pdf |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=South Australian Health and Medical Research Institute |pages=7|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231019233016/https://sahmri.blob.core.windows.net/communications/sahmri.org/Annual_Report_2014.pdf|archive-date=2023-10-19}}</ref> In January 2014, he approved construction of a new great hall as part of UniSA's City West Campus development on [[Hindley Street]], with the project comprising an underground hall, pool, student accommodation and a plaza adjoining the Jeffrey Smart Building.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-01-23 |title=UniSA to build underground 'Great Hall' in Hindley St |url=https://www.indailysa.com.au/news/archive/2014/01/23/exclusive-unisa-build-great-hall-hindley-st |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=InDaily|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260818004442/https://www.indailysa.com.au/news/archive/2014/01/23/exclusive-unisa-build-great-hall-hindley-st|archive-date=2026-08-18}}</ref> During 2014, he continued implementing UniSA's strategic and capital development programs, sought to increase international student numbers and opposed consolidation of South Australia's universities, arguing that a merger would create an overly large institution. His [[remuneration]] as vice chancellor increased from approximately $540,000–$550,000 in 2013 to $810,000–$820,000 in 2014; UniSA said the increase had been determined through sector benchmarking by the [[university council]].<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Tim |date=2015-07-14 |title=UniSA Vice-Chancellor David Lloyd receives pay rise of up to $280,000 |url=https://www.adelaidenow.com.au/news/south-australia/unisa-vicechancellor-david-lloyd-receives-pay-rise-of-up-to-280000/news-story/9250d1aa715d48e6dad723740f093e05?amp |url-access=subscription |access-date=2026-07-17 |website=The Advertiser}}</ref> In June, Lloyd was appointed to the state's 12-member [[Economic Development Board (South Australia)|Economic Development Board]], which advised on economic development.<ref name=":10" /> In August, he supported discussions about establishing a single commercial entity for the corporate arms of South Australia's three universities.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2014-08-19 |title=University welcomes recommendation of single commercial entity |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2014-08-19/university-welcomes-single-commercial-entity-recommendation/5680204 |access-date=2026-08-17 |work=[[ABC News (Australia)|ABC News]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161101040356/http://www.abc.net.au/news/2014-08-19/university-welcomes-single-commercial-entity-recommendation/5680204|archive-date=2016-11-01}}</ref> He also founded the Innovation and Collaboration Centre, a [[joint venture]] between UniSA, the [[Weatherill ministry|Weatherill government]] and [[Hewlett Packard Enterprise]] intended to support innovation, entrepreneurship and business development.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-11-16 |title=New centre to stimulate innovation in South Australia |url=https://www.ausleisure.com.au/news/new-centre-to-stimulate-innovation-in-south-australia |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=Australasian Leisure Management}}</ref>

In April 2015, UniSA rose from 49th to 35th among universities aged under 50 in the ''[[Times Higher Education]]'' University Rankings.<ref name=":9" /> Lloyd also promoted a proposal under which university fees would be announced five years in advance, with provision for subsequent reductions. In May, his appointment as vice chancellor was extended to 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hare |first=Julie |date=2015-05-15 |title=Lloyd to stay at UniSA until 2022 |url=https://www.theaustralian.com.au/higher-education/lloyd-to-stay-at-unisa-until-2022/news-story/02059ea640bf78c2f8ad540aafb3d9df?amp |url-access=subscription |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=The Australian}}</ref> In September, he facilitated a partnership between UniSA and China's Yabao Pharmaceutical Company to establish a [[drug discovery]] laboratory for cancer research.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kumar |first=Yasmita |date=2015-09-09 |title=Yabao Pharmaceutical and UniSA embark on joint venture |url=https://pharmafile.com/news/yabao-pharmaceutical-and-unisa-embark-joint-venture/ |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=Pharmafile|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260818004919/https://pharmafile.com/news/yabao-pharmaceutical-and-unisa-embark-joint-venture/|archive-date=2026-08-18}}</ref> That month, he announced that the [[David Unaipon College of Indigenous Education and Research]] would cease operating as a separate college at the end of the year, with its courses transferred to other UniSA campuses, following recommendations from a government-commissioned report published in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-09-15 |title=SA Indigenous college to close |url=https://www.sbs.com.au/news/article/sa-indigenous-college-to-close/jwrv4ntrf |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=[[SBS News]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250123191747/https://www.sbs.com.au/news/article/sa-indigenous-college-to-close/jwrv4ntrf|archive-date=2025-01-23}}</ref> The proposal prompted concern among [[Aboriginal South Australians|Aboriginal community members]] that integrating the programs into the wider university structure could reduce culturally safe services and environments. Lloyd said the institution-wide model would provide greater opportunities for Indigenous students and support increased Indigenous enrolments, including through the creation of an Indigenous pro vice-chancellor. Some Aboriginal representatives criticised the consultation process as insufficiently involving the local Indigenous community.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gage |first=Nicola |date=2015-09-16 |title=Indigenous school closure sparks concerns about 'mainstreamed' courses |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2015-09-16/indigenous-school-closure-provokes-anger-in-sa/6780802 |access-date=2026-08-17 |work=ABC News|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221229161825/https://www.abc.net.au/news/2015-09-16/indigenous-school-closure-provokes-anger-in-sa/6780802|archive-date=2022-12-29}}</ref> In October, Lloyd became involved in establishing the Sir [[Terry Pratchett]] Memorial Scholarship after a letter from Pratchett expressing his wish for such a scholarship was discovered and referred to Lloyd.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barter |first=Pavel |date=2015-10-18 |title=Pratchett leaves cash to colleges |url=https://www.thetimes.com/travel/destinations/australasia-travel/australia/pratchett-leaves-cash-to-colleges-cmv5jwwns6k |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=[[The Times]]}}</ref>

As vice chancellor, Lloyd's remuneration rose by 9% in 2016, from roughly $880,000 to $960,000.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Tim |date=2017-08-19 |title=UniSA boss David Lloyd received 9 per cent pay rise in 2016 to $960,000 |url=https://www.adelaidenow.com.au/news/south-australia/unisa-boss-david-lloyd-received-9-per-cent-pay-rise-in-2016-to-960000/news-story/437ee3527287ab7a4be1f4658f1b211b |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=The Advertiser|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170923201957/http://www.adelaidenow.com.au/news/south-australia/unisa-boss-david-lloyd-received-9-per-cent-pay-rise-in-2016-to-960000/news-story/437ee3527287ab7a4be1f4658f1b211b|archive-date=2017-09-23}}</ref> In May 2017, he supported the establishment of the [[Saab AB|Saab]] Australia–UniSA Institute for Defence Technologies through a partnership between the two organisations. Based at Saab Australia's [[Mawson Lakes, South Australia|Mawson Lakes]] headquarters, the institute was intended to provide industry-based education and research in systems engineering, engineering, information technology and related fields.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-05-04 |title=New Saab-UniSA Institute Building Next Generation Defence Skills in SA |url=https://www.saab.com/markets/australia/news/stories/2017/new-saab-unisa-institute-building-next-generation-defence-skills-in-sa |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=Saab|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260818005153/https://www.saab.com/markets/australia/news/stories/2017/new-saab-unisa-institute-building-next-generation-defence-skills-in-sa|archive-date=2026-08-18}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Waldhuter |first=Lauren |date=2017-05-04 |title=SAAB to create 200 jobs in Adelaide office expansion |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2017-05-04/saab-announces-expansion-of-adelaide-office/8496876 |access-date=2026-08-17 |work=ABC News|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170510101801/https://www.abc.net.au/news/2017-05-04/saab-announces-expansion-of-adelaide-office/8496876|archive-date=2017-05-10}}</ref> In October, Lloyd announced a three-year partnership between UniSA and the [[Adelaide Football Club]] covering both the [[Australian Football League|AFL]] and [[AFLW]] teams.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-10-16 |title=Crows and UniSA join forces |url=https://www.afc.com.au/news/304022/crows-and-unisa-join-forces |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=Adelaide Football Club|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260818005305/https://www.afc.com.au/news/304022/crows-and-unisa-join-forces|archive-date=2026-08-18}}</ref> In November, plans were announced for the $247 million Health Innovation Building on North Terrace. Designed under Lloyd's leadership, the building was to incorporate the Cancer Centre for Biology, the [[Museum of Discovery (Adelaide)|Museum of Discovery]] and the Innovation and Collaboration Centre.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Tim |date=2017-11-17 |title=Universities unite to put SA at the forefront of innovation, health and medical research |url=https://www.adelaidenow.com.au/smart-sa/sas-universities-unite-to-put-the-state-at-the-forefront-of-innovation-medical-and-health-research/news-story/800a3cb62a714a973d78aec654e3750b |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=The Advertiser|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171123042032/http://www.adelaidenow.com.au/smart-sa/sas-universities-unite-to-put-the-state-at-the-forefront-of-innovation-medical-and-health-research/news-story/800a3cb62a714a973d78aec654e3750b|archive-date=2017-11-23}}</ref>
[[File:Pridham Hall of Adelaide University City West Campus (028A1277).jpg|thumb|Pridham Hall main entrance in 2026]]
Lloyd remained a member of the Economic Development Board until 2018.<ref name=":5" /> In February 2018, UniSA completed its $50 million Pridham Hall on Hindley Street and took possession of the facility ahead of its first major event, a graduation ceremony scheduled for April.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Tim |date=2018-02-14 |title=First look inside UniSA's $50 million Pridham Hall on Hindley St |url=https://www.adelaidenow.com.au/news/south-australia/first-look-inside-unisas-50-million-pridham-hall-on-hindley-st/news-story/43e7d12fcfd7fe7bf33e21f2e2c02339?amp |url-access=subscription |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=The Advertiser}}</ref> In June, Lloyd initiated discussions concerning a possible merger between UniSA and the [[University of Adelaide]] (UofA), reviving a proposal that had been considered periodically since 2010. A six-month process was established to examine the potential benefits, threshold issues and strategic risks, with Lloyd supporting the proposal.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dodd |first=Tim |date=2018-06-20 |title=University merger plan stokes union's fears for jobs |url=https://www.theaustralian.com.au/higher-education/university-merger-plan-stokes-unions-fears-for-jobs/news-story/7d49c44d8b47a14c0e7b9db886bcb9a2?amp |url-access=subscription |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=The Australian}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2018-10-23 |title=South Australian universities decide against merger |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2018-10-23/unisa-and-adelaide-university-decide-against-merger/10418520 |access-date=2026-08-17 |work=ABC News|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260319131232/https://www.abc.net.au/news/2018-10-23/unisa-and-adelaide-university-decide-against-merger/10418520|archive-date=2026-03-19}}</ref> On 1 July, he was appointed to the [[Australian Research Council]] Advisory Council.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019 |title=Annual Report 2018–19 |url=https://www.arc.gov.au/system/files/2026-05/arc_annualreport_2018-19.pdf |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=Australian Research Council |pages=61|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260818005812/https://www.arc.gov.au/system/files/2026-05/arc_annualreport_2018-19.pdf|archive-date=2026-08-18}}</ref> In August, UniSA announced plans under its Enterprise25 strategy to redevelop the [[Magill, South Australia|Magill]] campus as an aged-care facility for training, research and practice development in partnership with an aged-care organisation.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-08-28 |title=UniSA plots $500M redevelopment with aged care training campus |url=https://www.theweeklysource.com.au/unisa-plots-500m-redevelopment-with-aged-care-training-campus/ |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=The Weekly Source|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181021012338/https://www.theweeklysource.com.au/unisa-plots-500m-redevelopment-with-aged-care-training-campus/|archive-date=2018-10-21}}</ref> In October, the merger discussions ended without agreement after the universities differed over key issues and risks. UofA subsequently confirmed that UniSA had decided not to continue negotiations. Lloyd said the UniSA Council had concluded that there was no compelling case for a merger and that the university would continue with its independent strategy.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Siebert |first=Bension |date=2021-01-21 |title=University of Adelaide texts, emails reveal backstory to merger breakdown |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-01-21/documents-shed-light-on-university-of-adelaide-sa-failed-merger/12960276 |access-date=2026-08-17 |work=ABC News|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260201034147/https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-01-21/documents-shed-light-on-university-of-adelaide-sa-failed-merger/12960276|archive-date=2026-02-01}}</ref>

In July 2019, UniSA announced a restructuring of its academic organisation under Lloyd's leadership, proposing to replace its 14 schools across four divisions, together with UniSA College, with seven academic units.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Tim |date=2019-07-19 |title=UniSA's biggest overhaul of its academic structure in 20 years |url=https://www.adelaidenow.com.au/news/south-australia/unisas-biggest-overhaul-of-its-academic-structure-in-20-years/news-story/23cd1cbd54e4b8206469e9bc14d5a71d?amp |url-access=subscription |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=The Advertiser}}</ref> In August, Lloyd was appointed chair of the [[Committee for Adelaide]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-08-28 |title=Media Release: Committee for Adelaide appoints new chair Professor David Lloyd |url=https://committeeforadelaide.org.au/media-release-committee-for-adelaide-appoints-new-chair-professor-david-lloyd/ |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=Committee For Adelaide|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260420160824/https://committeeforadelaide.org.au/media-release-committee-for-adelaide-appoints-new-chair-professor-david-lloyd/|archive-date=2026-04-20}}</ref> By 2021, UniSA had developed a course in collaboration with aged-care provider ACH and established an Enterprise Partnership Hub at [[Light Square]] to facilitate businesses' access to university research.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Russell |first=Chris |date=2021-02-09 |title=SA's 21 agenda setters of 2021: David Lloyd finds convergence between new technology and traditional industries |url=https://www.adelaidenow.com.au/news/south-australia/sas-21-agenda-setters-of-2021-david-lloyd-finds-convergence-between-new-technology-and-traditional-industries/news-story/c553b8a6c0cbe1d78404a027dd3b6992?amp |url-access=subscription |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=The Advertiser}}</ref> In an open letter, Lloyd characterised UniSA as a $700 million not-for-loss company employing more than 5,000 people; the characterisation was subsequently discussed in scholarly literature concerning the application of corporate efficiency and effectiveness principles to Australian universities.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Pelizzon |first=A. |last2=Joannes-Boyau |first2=R. |last3=Lake |first3=S. |last4=Lucas |first4=A. |last5=McCallum |first5=A. |last6=Noble |first6=D. |last7=O'Connor |first7=J. |last8=Orr |first8=J. |last9=Schröder-Turk |first9=G. |last10=Tregear |first10=P. |last11=Vodeb |first11=O. |display-authors=3 |date=2022 |title=Australian Public Universities: A crisis of governance |url=https://ap-st01.ext.exlibrisgroup.com/61USC_INST/upload/1786947065407/Australian%20Public%20Universities%20-%20A%20crisis%20of%20governance.pdf?AccessRightAllowDownload=true&Expires=1786947185&Signature=RqNIQnEPXc381NlPPhy9KQaJFU1l88QaXLXMVFs7LCScHVZEmsg-Aa5M-Ag~ugvPg3zAIvJDaY-fPOv4AKZXqpL20CAyh4D08iJ95oWmtw7njo5JCF1YvfhD~c6spS0NryFoHhuJ5R5p5MahL4PlrrGvhzzvP1ZfAh5Tkk2waK2inOVx0lHCYl4LBK0nbBAeTFbJWeqhzw~ALs7EYN43qyqVB2zlQPWgS823RqPp95FbFtqvwAKDhaN5XrV20rAG8mB6PpeGGpCsFtf64WpOUAB7QNNf90qVyYWg~NbCyTUW8Csz8cxTudhnT~vnRqdcA8c2lmWKRiyMLO4VfnVmZw__&Key-Pair-Id=APKAJ72OZCZ36VGVASIA |journal=Social Alternatives |publisher=[[University of Sunshine Coast]] |volume=41 |issue=1 |pages=22}}</ref> In June 2021, UniSA extended Lloyd's term as vice chancellor until December 2027, citing the university's 30-year anniversary and its Academic Enterprise Plan 2021–2025 under the Enterprise25 framework.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-06-28 |title=UniSA secures leadership team for future |url=https://www.miragenews.com/unisa-secures-leadership-team-for-future-586046/ |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=Mirage News}}</ref>

=== Adelaide University (2022–2026) ===
[[File:University of Adelaide and University of South Australia.jpg|left|thumb|Adelaide Health and Medical Sciences Building of UofA and Jeffrey Smart Building of UniSA in April 2025, prior to the merger]]
In December 2022, Lloyd and UofA vice chancellor Høj proposed merging UniSA and UofA to establish [[Adelaide University]] (AU). Lloyd said the proposed institution would develop its curriculum in consultation with business and the community, incorporate digital technology into its courses and expand enrolments through online study, including among mid-career students from other Australian states.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dodd |first=Tim |date=2022-12-13 |title=Digital education is the key to SA's university merger say vice-chancellors |url=https://www.theaustralian.com.au/higher-education/digital-education-is-the-key-to-sas-university-merger-say-vicechancellors/news-story/3221da49a8d6e42f5c98272b03da3302?amp |url-access=subscription |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=The Australian}}</ref> In March 2023, he proposed that companies could assist graduates with [[HECS-HELP]] debt through employment agreements linked to internships and advocated a government-backed, means-tested scholarship scheme for disadvantaged students, including mature-age students ineligible for [[Youth Allowance]].<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |last=Hare |first=Julie |date=2023-03-26 |title=Why don't companies pay employees' student loans, asks David Lloyd |url=https://www.afr.com/work-and-careers/education/why-don-t-companies-pay-employees-student-loans-asks-david-lloyd-20230316-p5csqc |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=[[Australian Financial Review]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250605031638/https://www.afr.com/work-and-careers/education/why-don-t-companies-pay-employees-student-loans-asks-david-lloyd-20230316-p5csqc|archive-date=2025-06-05}}</ref>

On 31 May 2023, Lloyd was confirmed as chair of [[Universities Australia]], succeeding [[John Dewar (academic)|John Dewar]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-05-31 |title=Universities Australia chair and board members confirmed |url=https://universitiesaustralia.edu.au/media-item/universities-australia-chair-and-board-members-confirmed/ |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=Universities Australia|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260419044455/https://universitiesaustralia.edu.au/media-item/universities-australia-chair-and-board-members-confirmed/|archive-date=2026-04-19}}</ref> In July, Lloyd and Høj were parties to the agreement under which the two universities proceeded with the merger. Both university councils approved the proposal, which received about $450 million in [[First Malinauskas ministry|Malinauskas government]] support for research and student assistance, the acquisition of UniSA properties and measures to attract international students. The universities committed to no compulsory redundancies or retrenchments resulting from the merger from its proposed commencement in January 2026 until 18 months afterwards. Under the December 2022 agreement, Lloyd and Høj were to serve as co-vice chancellors during the initial transition before an open competitive process to appoint a vice chancellor.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Starick |first=Paul |date=2023-07-01 |title=Historic merger of the universities of Adelaide and South Australia gets green light |url=https://www.adelaidenow.com.au/news/south-australia/historic-merger-of-the-universities-of-adelaide-and-south-australia-gets-green-light/news-story/63ae7a240da31e1fe619f7cb792b363c?amp&nk=9d6716e4ac3bc5a3c87c75458268cca2-1688213560 |url-access=subscription |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=The Advertiser}}</ref> On 8 March 2024, AU was established under the ''Adelaide University Act 2023'', with Lloyd and Høj serving as co-vice chancellors during the transition.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-28 |title=New Adelaide University receives formal registration |url=https://adelaide.edu.au/content/dam/adelaideuniversity/documents/about/news-and-events/pdfs/adelaide-university-receives-formal-registration.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260530065126/https://adelaide.edu.au/content/dam/adelaideuniversity/documents/about/news-and-events/pdfs/adelaide-university-receives-formal-registration.pdf |archive-date=2026-05-30 |access-date=2026-07-20 |website=Adelaide University}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-03-31 |title=Adelaide University Act 2023 |url=https://www.legislation.sa.gov.au/_legislation-documents/lz/c/a/adelaide-university-act-2023/current/2023.32.auth.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260520161547/https://www.legislation.sa.gov.au/_legislation-documents/lz/c/a/adelaide-university-act-2023/current/2023.32.auth.pdf |archive-date=2026-05-20 |access-date=2026-05-20 |website=South Australian Legislation |pages=32}}</ref> In April 2024, UniSA, the state government, defence industry representatives and the Australian Industry Group launched a degree apprenticeship program. Lloyd said the program would provide students with early experience in the South Australian defence industry and develop skills relevant to the sector; the government committed $450,000 over three years to the program.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-04-24 |title=UniSA inaugurates degree apprenticeship program |url=https://www.australiandefence.com.au/news/news/unisa-inaugurates-degree-apprenticeship-program |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=Australian Defence Magazine|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250722205811/https://www.australiandefence.com.au/news/news/unisa-inaugurates-degree-apprenticeship-program|archive-date=2025-07-22}}</ref>
[[File:David Lloyd at the September-October 2025 Graduation Ceremonies (University of South Australia).jpg|thumb|270x270px|Lloyd as chancellor at a graduation ceremony at Pridham Hall in 2025]]
In January 2025, Lloyd and Høj announced that neither would seek appointment as AU's inaugural substantive vice-chancellor, citing their roles in overseeing the merger and the need to avoid a [[conflict of interest]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kelsall |first=Thomas |date=2025-01-16 |title=Twist in Adelaide University vice-chancellor search |url=https://www.indailysa.com.au/news/in-depth/2025/01/16/international-consultancy-to-lead-adelaide-university-vice-chancellor-search |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260720002107/https://www.indailysa.com.au/news/in-depth/2025/01/16/international-consultancy-to-lead-adelaide-university-vice-chancellor-search |archive-date=2026-07-20 |access-date=2026-07-20 |work=InDaily}}</ref> Following an international recruitment process, [[Nicola Phillips]] was appointed (second) vice-chancellor and president<ref>{{Cite web |title=SA Government welcomes announcement of new Vice Chancellor to Adelaide University |url=https://www.premier.sa.gov.au/media-releases/news-archive/sa-government-welcomes-announcement-of-new-vice-chancellor-to-adelaide-university |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251201065011/https://www.premier.sa.gov.au/media-releases/news-archive/sa-government-welcomes-announcement-of-new-vice-chancellor-to-adelaide-university |archive-date=2025-12-01 |access-date=2026-07-20 |website=Government of South Australia}}</ref> and commenced on 12 January 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Adelaide University appoints new Vice Chancellor |url=https://adelaide.edu.au/about/news/2025/Adelaide-University-appoints-new-Vice-Chancellor/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260516181851/https://adelaide.edu.au/about/news/2025/Adelaide-University-appoints-new-Vice-Chancellor/ |archive-date=2026-05-16 |access-date=2026-07-20 |website=Adelaide University}}</ref> In May 2025, Lloyd told a South Australian [[parliamentary committee]] that 2,767 UniSA staff had transferred to AU through the merger, leaving him as the only remaining employee on the UniSA payroll. He also raised concerns about the effects of a proposed cap on international student numbers and visa costs on future enrolments. The estimated cost of the merger was reported at between $500 million and $650 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Willis |first=Belinda |date=2025-05-19 |title=Adelaide University merger leaves Prof David Lloyd as UniSA lone staffer on $1m salary |url=https://www.adelaidenow.com.au/south-australia-education/adelaide-university-merger-leaves-prof-david-lloyd-as-unisa-lone-staffer-on-1m-salary/news-story/74e8b7995ee4b4f62086989f7d337a5d?amp&nk=42a557825b4ddb361d63711fef0091d0-1747667814 |url-access=subscription |archive-date= |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=The Advertiser}}</ref> Lloyd's term as chair of Universities Australia ended on 29 May 2025, when he was succeeded by [[Carolyn Evans]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-29 |title=New Universities Australia chair and board members confirmed |url=https://universitiesaustralia.edu.au/media-item/new-universities-australia-chair-and-board-members-confirmed/ |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=Universities Australia|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260720001651/https://universitiesaustralia.edu.au/media-item/new-universities-australia-chair-and-board-members-confirmed/|archive-date=2026-07-20}}</ref> On 19 November, Lloyd was appointed to the board of governors of St Andrew's Hospital in Adelaide.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-11-19 |title=Welcoming New Voices to Our Board of Governors |url=https://www.stand.org.au/articles/welcoming-new-voices-to-our-board-of-governors |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=St Andrews Hospital|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260316075547/https://www.stand.org.au/articles/welcoming-new-voices-to-our-board-of-governors|archive-date=2026-03-16}}</ref> In that same month, Lloyd and Høj appeared before an [[Australian Senate]] inquiry into university governance, where they discussed the merger, regulatory requirements and the integration of staff and operations.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gilchrist |first=Charlie |date=2025-11-10 |title=Uni vice chancellors grilled over 'unprecedented' merger |url=https://www.indailysa.com.au/news/just-in/2025/11/10/sa-uni-vice-chancellors-grilled-over-unprecedented-merger |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260711084203/https://www.indailysa.com.au/news/just-in/2025/11/10/sa-uni-vice-chancellors-grilled-over-unprecedented-merger |archive-date=2026-07-11 |access-date=2026-07-20 |work=InDaily}}</ref> A farewell ceremony for Lloyd was held by [[Governor of South Australia|Governor]] [[Frances Adamson]] on 6 February 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-06 |title=Farewell Dinner for Professor David Lloyd, Vice Chancellor and President, University of South Australia |url=https://www.governor.sa.gov.au/vice-regal/speeches/farewell-dinner-for-professor-david-lloyd-vice-chancellor-and-president-university-of-south-australia |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=[[Government House, Adelaide|Government House Adelaide]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260815174013/https://www.governor.sa.gov.au/vice-regal/speeches/farewell-dinner-for-professor-david-lloyd-vice-chancellor-and-president-university-of-south-australia|archive-date=2026-08-15}}</ref>

In July 2026, AU Council stated that Lloyd's remuneration for 2025 and 2026 had not met community expectations. An auditor-general's report tabled in the [[South Australian Parliament]] recorded total remuneration of $3.112 million for Lloyd in 2025, comprising a base salary of $1.015 million, $209,000 in [[superannuation]], a $1.128 million merger-related termination payment and about $760,000 in performance pay and long-service leave payments.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hill |first=Aden |date=2026-07-09 |title=Adelaide University says former VC's $3.1m pay packet 'doesn't meet community expectations' |url=https://www.adelaidenow.com.au/education/regions/south-australia/adelaide-university-says-former-vcs-31m-pay-packet-doesnt-meet-community-expectations/news-story/3c3d7d2def82a0311888c39403a91cea?amp |url-access=subscription |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=The Advertiser}}</ref> The reported 2025 remuneration represented a 138 per cent increase from the $1.303 million he received in 2024 as UniSA vice chancellor and AU co-vice chancellor. Lloyd received a further $1.451 million payment in 2026 after leaving university management following completion of the merger. [[Minister for Education (Australia)|Education Minister]] [[Jason Clare]] criticised the $1.128 million termination payment and sought an explanation from the former UniSA council. AU stated that Lloyd's and Høj's remuneration arrangements had been determined by the respective university councils.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Truu |first=Maani |date=2026-07-08 |title='Gobsmacking': Clare demands answers over $1.1m uni golden handshake |url=https://www.afr.com/policy/health-and-education/gobsmacking-clare-demands-answers-over-1-1m-uni-golden-handshake-20260708-p60dke |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=Australian Financial Review|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260709150503/https://www.afr.com/policy/health-and-education/gobsmacking-clare-demands-answers-over-1-1m-uni-golden-handshake-20260708-p60dke|archive-date=2026-07-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ross |first=John |date=2026-07-06 |title=Merger university v-c gets A$1.1m golden handshake |url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/merger-university-v-c-gets-a11m-golden-handshake |url-access=subscription |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=[[Times Higher Education]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260709154600/https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/merger-university-v-c-gets-a11m-golden-handshake|archive-date=2026-07-09}}</ref>

== Later career ==
Following his departure from AU, Lloyd established BlueRange Advisory, a consulting firm providing independent strategic advice on organisational and institutional change.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bita |first=Natasha |date=2026-07-10 |title=University of SA chief David Lloyd's $4.5m payout sparks federal crackdown |url=https://www.theaustralian.com.au/higher-education/university-of-sa-chief-david-lloyds-45m-payout-sparks-federal-crackdown/news-story/5579942bc6888476ff16ca824342970f?amp |url-access=subscription |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=The Australian}}</ref> As of 2026, he is a presiding member of Super SA.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Leadership Team |url=https://www.supersa.sa.gov.au/about-us/leadership-team/ |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=Super SA|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260317034735/https://www.supersa.sa.gov.au/about-us/leadership-team/|archive-date=2026-03-17}}</ref>

He commenced as Interim Vice Chancellor of the University of Notre Dame Australia on Monday 28 September 2026, and will continue until the incoming Vice Chancellor commences in the role.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dame |first=Notre |date=2026-09-21 |title=Appointment of Interim Vice Chancellor |url=https://www.notredame.edu.au/news-items/appointment-of-interim-vice-chancellor |access-date=2026-09-23 |website=Notre Dame |language=en}}</ref>

==Honours and recognitions==
[[File:Lloyd Building at Adelaide University's City West campus in September 2026 (028A1024).jpg|thumb|The Lloyd Building at Light Square, Adelaide in September 2026]]
In 2008, Lloyd was elected a fellow of Trinity College Dublin.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2009-05-08 |title=Trinity Monday 2008 - Fellows and Scholars |url=https://www.tcd.ie/Secretary/FellowsScholars/2008/index.php |access-date=2025-12-29 |website=Trinity College Dublin |archive-date=2016-04-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160414170412/http://www.tcd.ie/Secretary/FellowsScholars/2008/index.php |url-status= }}</ref> He is also a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry]] and an honorary professor at Tianjin University.<ref name=":4" /> In 2019, he was elected a [[List of fellows of the Australian Academy of Technological Sciences and Engineering|Fellow of the Australian Academy of Technological Sciences and Engineering]] (FTSE).<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |last= |date=2023-05-31 |title=Professor David Lloyd |url=https://www.atse.org.au/who-we-are/our-fellows/all-fellows/david-lloyd/ |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=Australian Academy of Technological Sciences and Engineering|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251208102056/https://www.atse.org.au/who-we-are/our-fellows/all-fellows/david-lloyd/|archive-date=2025-12-08}}</ref> In November 2025, UniSA's Enterprise Hub building at Light Square was renamed the Lloyd Building in recognition of his service as the university's vice-chancellor.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-07-15 |title='Insulting': Landmark building to be named after uni chief with multimillion-dollar payday |url=https://www.indailysa.com.au/news/just-in/2026/07/15/insulting-landmark-building-to-be-named-after-uni-chief-with-multimillion-dollar-payday |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=InDaily|last=Gilchrist|first=Charlie|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260818022831/https://www.indailysa.com.au/news/just-in/2026/07/15/insulting-landmark-building-to-be-named-after-uni-chief-with-multimillion-dollar-payday|archive-date=2026-08-18}}</ref> In March 2026 Lloyd was conferred with an honorary doctorate and an emeritus professorship by UniSA.

== Personal life ==
In 1995, Lloyd met his future wife, Annie Timlin, while they were both working at Waltons.<ref name=":3" /> He performed in bands and played several instruments, including guitar, keyboard, [[mandolin]] and [[hammered dulcimer]].<ref name=":3" /> Lloyd has two adult children from his first marriage. He remarried, to Penny, in 2025. Lloyd was a friend of author Pratchett<ref name=":0" /> and wrote a review of Pratchett's ''The Shepherd's Crown'' in 2015, stating that they had been friends since 2008.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lloyd |first=David G. |date=2015-08-31 |title=Shepherd's Crown is a crowning achievement for Terry Pratchett and his Discworld |url=https://theconversation.com/shepherds-crown-is-a-crowning-achievement-for-terry-pratchett-and-his-discworld-46872 |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=[[The Conversation (website)|The Conversation]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251002210559/https://theconversation.com/shepherds-crown-is-a-crowning-achievement-for-terry-pratchett-and-his-discworld-46872|archive-date=2025-10-02}}</ref> He was also awarded an honorary Doctor of Unseen University, the fictional institution featured in Pratchett's novels.<ref name=":4" /> In October 2024 [[Penguin Random House|Penguin]] [https://terrypratchett.com/news/terry-pratchett-penguin-classic/ announced] Lloyd as one of two contributing co-authors for the new introduction and annotations of the [[Penguin Modern Classic|Modern Classics]] edition of Pratchett's bestselling novel, [[Night Watch (Pratchett novel)|Night Watch]].
